name: teinm laeda

attributes.attribute: Irish divination by touching or holding an object
gained the gift by sucking his thumb

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Teinm laeda was a form of divination used in ancient Ireland. The report likens it to what is now called a reading of objects. The seeker touched or held a thing in their hands. A verse or a ritual phrase was said first. The druid could then touch the object with a stick of hazel. The truth about the object was then read from the touch. The hero Fionn mac Cumhaill is said to have gained such skill by chewing his thumb. The practice was banned, like the trance method.

okr.objective: Record teinm laeda as an ancient Irish form of divination.
key_results: Explains the rite as a form of revelation by touch
States that druids used a rod of hazel
States it was banned with the trance method
